speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It is a timely reminder to consider how we can better prepare Singapore to be a dementia-friendly society.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In time to come, there will be more senior citizens and they will live longer, too.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The downside is that with more older people, there will also be more people afflicted with dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The incidence rate will increase to one out of two for those above age 85.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Is Singapore ready to cope with more people living with dementia?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: More importantly, can Singapore be a more dementia-friendly society as this disease becomes more prevalent in our rapidly-ageing society?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Dementia is a terminal illness because people living with dementia, or PLWDs in short, will not recover.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In the advanced stage, most PLWDs would require extensive caregiving needs.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Caregiving for PLWDs is challenging and may require 24/7 attention.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Very often, family members will have to give up their work and some may even suffer from burnout.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: There will be also implications for the caregivers' own financial security in old age and the productivity of our labour force will also take a hit.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The economic impact to the families and society at large cannot be underestimated.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: On this note, I would like to ask the Ministry if a comprehensive study on the social and economic impact of dementia on Singapore can be commissioned.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Fortunately, my family members have been able to rally together to support one another and we are fortunate to have access to help and support.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, for many Singaporeans, they may have great difficulty coping with caregiving for a loved one afflicted with dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In fact, I have met several residents who are struggling to cope with caregiving.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They shared that due to lack of social interaction during the pandemic, their loved ones who are afflicted with dementia have shown significant cognitive decline and deterioration of their motor skills.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In recent years, there have been concerted efforts to increase awareness and provide community support services to help families with PLWDs.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I sincerely appreciate the efforts made by the Government and various community groups, voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) and volunteers to assist PLWDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Nonetheless, we are racing against time as there is a fast-closing window to get ready before the dementia emergency hits us.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I urge the Government to expedite the implementation of dementia-focused policies and the building of more dementia-friendly infrastructure and community programmes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As details regarding future measures for dementia was not quite covered in the recent Healthier SG White Paper, I would like to share my ideas in this Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I will start with building capacity which takes the longest lead time; then mitigation against challenges associated with dementia; and finally, prevention.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Many of the suggestions and feedback are collated from community partners whom I work with.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to express my appreciation and gratitude to the staff, volunteers and families who had shared their thoughts and suggestions with me.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I hope to carry their voices in this House so that, as a society, Singapore can be better prepared for dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Capacity projection for dementia care is a challenging task because the needs of PLWDs are wide-ranging and complex.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: There are different types of dementia and the health conditions for PLWDs at different stages of dementia can vary across a wide spectrum.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: A range of care facilities are needed to provide comprehensive care for PLWDs and to support their caregivers.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Capacity building can be broadly discussed in two categories, namely, medical facilities and expertise, as well as community facilities and programmes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Over the years, the Government has been building up its capacity in the provision of primary care.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I look forward to mental health and memory clinics being available in all polyclinics so that PLWDs can access these facilities quite conveniently.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I urge the Ministry to consider including dementia detection as an option for seniors undergoing regular health screening.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Early diagnostics and detection are critical to help patients slow down the progress of dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It is very important to catch this disease early because there is only a small window to intervene effectively through a beneficial combination of medication, exercise, brain stimulation and socialisation.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In terms of trained medical personnel, I also hope that MOH has been increasing the number of geriatricians and psychologists.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: How will MOH build up this pipeline of medical specialists over the next eight years?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Ageing-in-place is the preferred way for PLWDs to live.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Familiarity with the living environment will help them cope better as their memory fades.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, for families that are unable to provide caregiving or for PLWDs who do not have loved ones to care for them, admission into nursing homes then becomes inevitable.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In the community, the number of places in dementia day care centres, senior care centres and nursing homes have been increasing.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I hope the Minister would share the progress on the infrastructure build-up plans and strategies to recruit staff and train them.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Also, how will we ramp up our caregiver support and training?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Would the Ministry elaborate on how these options will be financed, Government subsidies available and the estimated range that a family is expected to pay?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Other than nursing homes, having a range of care and accommodation options is key to support families who are struggling with family members with dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: While some PLWDs may need 24/7 full-time care, some others will actually be able to manage a range of independent living with varying levels of support or supervision.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hence, it is important to provide alternative models of care in the community for PLWDs, other than nursing homes and senior day care centres, such as the Wellness Kampung community facilities, where they can participate in social activities while their caregivers get some respite.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As our nation enters into an ageing demographic phase, it is crucial to review the design of our estates.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our estates will have to be more dementia-friendly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I would encourage fellow Members of Parliament and their Town Councils to consider adopting dementia-friendly designs for their repainting works.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Distinctive colours and landmarks can be created to help PLWDs to better recognise their surroundings in case they lose their bearings and are unable to find their way home.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Another idea is to proliferate assisted living arrangements which allow seniors to remain independent and socially connected.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This would also address the issue of many elderly living alone after their children get married and move out.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: One such example is Red Crown social enterprise, which arranges for several seniors to live together, provide companionship and help to take care of one another.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Some degree of Government involvement and grants can help to scale up this nascent industry and to ensure that operators meet minimum service standards.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: VWOs play a key role to assist PLWDs and their caregivers.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They have well-trained social workers and volunteers to engage PLWDs in social activities that will slow down their decline and calm their moods.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They also assist caregivers with counselling services so that they can manage their stress better and deal with burnout.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Unfortunately, many families with PLWDs are not even aware of the services provided by these VWOs.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Hence, the community network plays an important role to connect the VWOs with residents who may need assistance.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The caregivers can also give each other mutual support and share their experiences and useful tips on caregiving.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, many of such VWOs are only partially funded by the Government and will need to raise their own funds, competing with other VWOs for the charity dollar.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To this end, a robust policy framework and adequate social infrastructure and services are essential for PLWDs to carry on with the basic functions to work, live and travel.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To protect the interests of PLWDs, we need to increase awareness of Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Advance Medical Directive (AMD).

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I urge the Ministry to consider increasing the visibility of LPAs, ACPs and AMDs at GPs, polyclinics as well as public and private hospitals.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: People should be more aware of the role of social workers and professional donees registered with the Office of the Public Guardian and agencies, such as the Special Needs Trust Company, a non-profit agency which helps vulnerable people set up care plans using their insurance or assets.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To create more awareness, we need more talks and seminars at the community level as well as coverage on our free-to-air TV channels and Government social media on dementia and what to do in preparation.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: For instance, the media coverage on several high-profile cases related to vulnerable PLWDs being swindled by ill-intended relatives or friends had actually spurred people to set up LPAs and wills.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Beyond the Government and local communities, I would also like to suggest more involvement of the private sector.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The public sector can collaborate with private entities to sponsor programmes within their companies and in the community to be dementia-friendly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our transportation system, airport, malls and public building owners can incorporate features to make their spaces and customer interactions more dementia-friendly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Similarly, service providers, particularly banks, need to consider how they can better serve these customers while protecting their interests.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It would be ideal if businesses can initiate these improvements.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Notwithstanding, I hope the Government would consider expediting these changes with guidelines and, if necessary, legislation for specific sectors.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: How can YODs remain employed for as long as possible?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: How can employers be incentivised to redesign job roles, offer micro jobs and shape a more dementia-friendly work environment?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Also, how can employers be more understanding and supportive towards employed caregivers who are supporting loved ones at home with dementia?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I hope a more compassionate and inclusive workplace culture would develop over time, especially as retirement age is progressively extended to 70.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In recent years, dementia has become more prevalent in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The centre will conduct research to understand more about this disease.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: A recent study published in the International Journal of Epidemiology suggests that obesity may be associated with an increased risk for developing dementia.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: While all of the above preventive actions are individual choices, the outcomes will have a profound impact on our families, our community and our nation.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Thus, we must all make a greater concerted effort to help one another make good choices for our health and to persist in them.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It will save individuals and the healthcare system a whole lot of money from medical bills and expenses in the future.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: For example, our hawker centres and food courts are still serving mostly high carbs, meaty dishes with little vegetables.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We will need to have more healthy choices for our national canteens and encourage people to consume more greens on top of less sugar, less salt and less oil.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: It has also been found in a recent Harvard Medical School study that the lack of sleep in middle-age persons may increase dementia risk.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Many of us, including my Parliamentary colleagues, sacrifice sleep to get more work done or to complete other tasks.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: One tell-tale sign of sleep deprivation is when Members occasionally nod off involuntarily in this Chamber.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Let us set a good example and get at least six to eight hours of sleep daily.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In the next decade, a lot more work needs to be done to increase our capacity, to mitigate the challenges associated with dementia and to take preventive lifestyle changes.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: While MOH expedites capacity building, we can all do our part to spread awareness about dementia, to improve our community facilities and programmes and also to take better care of ourselves while we are still young.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Let us not burden our future generations with the challenges of caregiving.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Most importantly, let us work towards a more compassionate, caring and inclusive society to help people living with dementia live with meaning and dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is an important topic, given our ageing population and the rising number of persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond healthcare, I will also share how MOH has collaborated with different agencies, community groups and businesses to build more caring and dementia-inclusive communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Adopting a healthy lifestyle can reduce the risk of dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through Healthier SG, we will empower our population to improve their health, such as through regular exercise and healthy eating.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, programmes like functional screening also allow us to identify seniors with hearing impairment and fit them with hearing aids.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This enables seniors to maintain social engagement with others which helps to lower the risk of dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Health Promotion Board (HPB) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) conduct campaigns and provide resources through portals like HealthHub and DementiaHub.SG to educate the public on common risk factors and signs of dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through education, we hope to destigmatise dementia and encourage early help-seeking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Early detection of dementia is important so that individuals receive timely treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nevertheless, there is no clear evidence internationally that general dementia screening in persons without recognised signs or symptoms of cognitive impairment is an effective public health intervention.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Hence, our current efforts in early detection continue to be targeted at those at risk.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Within the community, we have outreach teams known as CREST that proactively identify seniors at risk of dementia and refer them for assessment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They have reached out to over 510,000 participants through outreach events and provided assistance to more than 32,000 persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Active ageing centres (AACs), polyclinics and trained general practitioners (GPs) also help to identify seniors with suspected dementia and refer them for assessment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These cases will be referred to memory clinics in polyclinics and hospitals to confirm the diagnosis and cause of dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More than half of our polyclinics currently provide these services and we are in discussions to bring more polyclinics on board.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Various care services support persons at different stages of dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The majority of dementia cases have mild to moderate needs and can be supported in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also have Community Intervention Teams (COMIT) that provide psychosocial interventions like counselling and case management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In FY2021, COMIT teams supported a total of 11,100 clients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A small group of dementia cases may require inpatient care as their condition deteriorates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The majority of nursing homes can care for persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: From end-2015, we have added 4,000 nursing home beds to reach a total of over 16,000 beds in end-2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Upcoming nursing homes developed by MOH are also built with dementia-friendly provisions like therapeutic gardens and closed-loop wandering paths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member stated that the current wait time for a nursing home bed is nine months to a year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To clarify, the median wait time is currently around one month, although this may take longer for some seniors who have specialised care needs or specific preferences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member asked about our pipeline of clinical manpower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, all doctors are trained to provide basic management of dementia conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Specialists like geriatricians and psychiatrists are equipped to manage more severe conditions associated with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This represents a 50% and 15% increase respectively from 2017.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This translates to 2.8 geriatricians and 5.1 psychiatrists per 100,000 population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There is no international consensus on the optimal ratio of geriatricians and psychiatrists to population.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH has also been increasing the number of residency training positions for geriatric medicine and psychiatrists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to review and adjust the pipeline of medical specialists to support ageing population needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We provide multiple layers of financial support to ensure that long-term care costs remain affordable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Lastly, MediFund will provide support for those who need further help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As announced earlier this year, we will also enhance the Home Caregiving Grant to defray caregiving costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Social Services Agencies (SSAs) play a key role in providing long-term care services and support for caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides direct funding for programmes and services, the Government also provides dollar-for-dollar matching grants for donations to SSAs through the Community Silver Trust.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member asked about support for: (a) caregivers of newly-diagnosed individuals; (b) caregiver training; and (c) working caregivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to review how to better support caregiver training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For working caregivers, MOM has worked with the tripartite partners to encourage the adoption of flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, a vast majority of employees have access to FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Caregivers can also tap on various community care options for their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include DDCs and the Night Respite Care pilot for those experiencing sun-downing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the Member pointed out, persons with dementia face complex challenges, such as safety and mental capacity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We must take a whole-of-society approach to address these issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2016, AIC launched the Dementia-Friendly Singapore (DFSG) initiative to establish more dementia-friendly communities (DFCs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Within a DFC, networks are created where residents, businesses and grassroots leaders are trained to look out for persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Go-to-Points (GTPs) are also created to serve as "safe return" points for those who might be lost.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: AIC will be launching a dementia campaign next month to rally more community and corporate partners to join us in making Singapore more dementia-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will expand our efforts to five sectors that regularly serve seniors, namely: transport, building, arts and leisure, banking and retail.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides transport, venues for the arts have also started catering programmes for persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2016, Esplanade launched the "Sing Out Loud!" programme to help persons with dementia deepen engagements with their caregivers through singing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, Esplanade also became the first arts venue to become a dementia Go-To-Point (GTP) and their staff also received basic training to assist visitors with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Creating a dementia-friendly physical environment is important for persons with dementia to move around safely and participate in social activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, Nee Soon Town Council worked with stakeholders to paint HDB blocks with large block numbers and contrasting colours to help residents with wayfinding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: AIC is also working with Centre of Liveable Cities (CLC) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) to study dementia-friendly neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The learnings gathered will be developed into a set of design guidelines to make the built environment safer and easier to navigate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HDB will continue to explore incorporating such dementia-friendly features into new developments and in existing estates through upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member also asked about micro-jobs for persons with dementia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH and MOM will work with tripartite partners like Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) and NTUC to enhance the understanding of dementia at the workplace through educational materials and encourage employers to hire such persons where they are able to meet the operational needs of businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Persons with dementia may find it increasingly difficult to make decisions independently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Seniors with mild dementia or even those who are well should plan ahead when they still have mental capacity, to give themselves and their loved ones peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH, MSF and PSD are working to increase awareness and adoption of instruments, such as the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and Advance Care Planning (ACP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We launched the My Legacy portal in 2020 to raise awareness on planning ahead and serve as a one-stop portal for end-of-life related matters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It contains an LPA-ACP tool which allows users to make both documents at one go.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This complements communications and engagement efforts, such as the annual ACP week campaign led by AIC, and involving our health and community care partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have made good progress and will continue to study further strategies to enhance dementia care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Let us work together to build a dementia-inclusive Singapore and support persons with dementia to lead purposeful and dignified lives.
